    - article:
      - 'heading "Definition: Best Under a Denominator Cap" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: For target α and budget Q, p/q is best if its chosen error is smallest among reduced fractions with 1 ≤ q ≤ Q.
      - paragraph: As Q grows, the record error can only decrease or stay the same.
    - article:
      - heading "Misconception warning" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Misconception warning
      - text: “Smallest absolute error” without a denominator limit is not a finite search.
      - paragraph: Arbitrarily large denominators allow arbitrarily small errors. Fair comparisons require a cap Q.
    - article:
      - heading "Metric matters" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Absolute error is |α − p/q|. Second-kind error is |qα − p| = q|α − p/q|.
      - button "Compare metrics side-by-side":
        - img
        - text: Compare metrics side-by-side
    - article:
      - 'heading "Compare: 22/7 vs 3.14 vs 355/113 (π)" [level=2]'
      - table:
        - rowgroup:

        - rowgroup:

      - paragraph: 355/113 is about 5,970 times more accurate than 3.14.
    - article:
      - 'heading "Why convergents win: Ford circles" [level=2]'
      - paragraph: The circle at reduced p/q has center (p/q, 1/(2q²)) and radius 1/(2q²).
      - img "True-scale Ford circles from 3 to 4 for denominators 1 to 7": 3 3.25 3.5 3.75 4
      - paragraph: Convergents provide excellent approximations; intermediate fractions may also set absolute-error records.
